title: Hanoi traffic police trace a missing 78-year-old on the city's new AI camera network; a passer-by finds him hypoglycemic in Dịch Vọng at 3 a.m.
summary: Hanoi police traced a lost 78-year-old on AI traffic cameras on 15 December 2025; a passer-by found him at 3 a.m. the next day and took him home.
account: Hanoi's AI traffic-camera network began official operation on 13 December 2025. Mr. Đ.V.T., 78, of Thanh Xuân ward, Hanoi, went out to exercise at 3:30 p.m. on 15 December 2025 and did not return. At 8:15 p.m. his family reported him to Thanh Xuân Ward Police. Ward officers worked with the Hanoi Traffic Police Department. Major Nguyễn Tá Khanh's team there searched the AI traffic-camera system in the direction that the family gave. It traced him along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and other streets. VietNamNet and Tiền Phong say that the images were posted on social media. At about 3 a.m. on 16 December a passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng, hypoglycemic and close to fainting, and took him home. No source links the finder to the camera trace or to the social-media appeal. Sức khỏe & Đời sống reports that the family said that his health was stable and that they sent thanks to the police and residents. By 29 June 2026 Hanoi had nearly 5,000 AI cameras.
purpose: Hanoi's AI traffic-camera system has 1,837 cameras with AI-controlled signals and was due to enter official operation in December 2025, per VOV. The Traffic Police run it, in VOV's words, “to ensure security and order and support the people” as well as to manage traffic. Tracing a lost resident for a ward police search falls within that stated remit.
system: Hanoi Traffic Police AI traffic-camera system (1,837 cameras)
deployer: Hanoi City Police, Traffic Police Department (Phòng Cảnh sát giao thông), with Thanh Xuân Ward Police
segment: Missing elderly person traced on urban traffic cameras
taxonomy_note: Tracing a lost elderly man is read as a rescue; a passer-by made the actual find.

ratings.reason: After nearly twelve hours out on a December night, the 78-year-old was found at about 3 a.m. in Dịch Vọng, hypoglycemic and close to fainting, and was taken home. His family said that his health was stable afterward, so a serious harm was averted in time. No source links the find to the police trace.
The camera trace gave Thanh Xuân Ward Police and the Traffic Police a direction of travel and images for the search. The police present the case as evidence of the new system's value.

ai_role.statement: The system's contribution was the trace. Police searched it in the direction the family gave. It returned images of the man walking along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and across other streets. That gave the police a route and pictures for a public appeal. A passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng about six hours and 45 minutes after the report. No source says the finder had seen the appeal or that officers reached him. So the discovery itself is not attributable to the system. The vendor is not named and every account comes from the police.
